label: Simulation, not a prediction

population.source: data/population.json (Track D synthetic population; each seed samples a subset)
population.note: The simulator evaluates a policy on a fictional night. It does not validate predictions about real households.

assumptions.name: Optimizer time limit per re-plan
assumptions.why: keeps 100 seeds under about 15 minutes; the production service uses 3 s, so the optimizer here is slightly weaker than deployed

assumptions.name: Re-plan cadence
assumptions.value: on arrival (debounced 90 s), when a vehicle frees up, and at least every 5 min
assumptions.why: mirrors the plan's debounced event-driven loop

assumptions.name: Solver objective weights (imported from solver.py)
assumptions.value: WAIT_COST_PER_WEIGHT_SECOND=1, LATENESS_COST_PER_SECOND=10, CHANGED_OFFER_COST=600, DROP_COST_SCALE=1000000
assumptions.why: read from the solver module at run time, so this list always matches the objective that produced the numbers

assumptions.name: Planning window
assumptions.value: the 40 pending requests with the earliest deadlines go to each dispatcher
assumptions.why: both dispatchers get the same window; only the first trip of each route is committed, and a short solver budget cannot handle 100+ requests

assumptions.name: Frozen runs
assumptions.value: each idle vehicle commits to the first trip of its returned route
assumptions.why: an accepted run is never moved or extended; later trips are re-planned from the run's end

assumptions.name: Driver cancellation
assumptions.value: 3% per committed pickup
assumptions.why: small stand-in rate; the request goes back to the open pool

assumptions.name: Dialer rate
assumptions.value: 1 new call per second, unlimited phone lines
assumptions.why: the plan says about 1 per second

assumptions.name: Answered call length
assumptions.value: 2 to 4 min, uniform
assumptions.why: from the plan

assumptions.name: Unanswered ring
assumptions.why: a ring or voicemail ends well before a conversation would

assumptions.name: Retries after no answer
assumptions.value: 2 min after the first miss, then 3 min after that (5 min total)
assumptions.why: the plan says retry at 2 and 5 minutes

assumptions.name: Text reply
assumptions.value: about 45% of households can reply; delay is lognormal with median 6 min; text gives up after 15 min
assumptions.why: stand-in; the door-check queue takes everyone left

assumptions.name: Door checks
assumptions.value: 6 teams, deadline-first, travel on the road graph plus 6 to 10 min per visit
assumptions.why: from the plan (about 8 min a visit)

assumptions.name: Call accuracy
assumptions.value: a reached household reports its true need
assumptions.why: perfect accuracy is optimistic; call accuracy is evaluated separately by Track D

assumptions.name: Answer probability
assumptions.value: per-household answersPhone, scaled by the answer-rate setting
assumptions.why: stand-in persona draw as in convex/seed.ts

assumptions.name: 911 callers
assumptions.value: 55% of households that need a ride call 911
assumptions.why: assumption for today's process; the Eaton Fire case shows long gaps before calls

assumptions.name: 911 call timing
assumptions.value: fire arrival minus a lognormal lead (median 20 min, clipped 5 to 90 min)
assumptions.why: people call when the fire is visibly near; assumption

assumptions.name: 911 call takers
assumptions.value: 2 takers, 2 to 4 min per call
assumptions.why: a queue models 'we have a lot of calls in that area'

assumptions.name: Radio delay before a unit moves
assumptions.value: 2 to 6 min, uniform
assumptions.why: assumption for today's process

assumptions.name: Today's dispatch rule
assumptions.value: first come first served, nearest idle unit, one rider per trip, no need matching
assumptions.why: an incompatible unit arrives, cannot load the rider, and the request goes back in line without that unit

assumptions.name: Deadline
assumptions.value: fire arrival at the home minus 10 min
assumptions.why: same as deadlineFor in convex/model.ts

assumptions.name: Primary metric
assumptions.value: pickups finished by the deadline
assumptions.why: a pickup finished after the deadline but before the fire arrives counts as late; after that, never picked up

assumptions.name: Hazard closures
assumptions.value: a road closes when the fire front reaches its midpoint
assumptions.why: the same front timing that sets household deadlines; recomputed every 10 min

assumptions.name: Travel times
assumptions.value: free-flow edge seconds from OpenStreetMap; a leg's time is fixed when it starts
assumptions.why: closures affect legs that start after them; riders already aboard are never stranded

assumptions.name: Unload time
assumptions.value: 120 s per arrival at the shelter
assumptions.why: same constant as the solver

assumptions.name: Shelter
assumptions.value: Pasadena Convention Center, capacity treated as unlimited
assumptions.why: 1200 is far above the number of riders

assumptions.name: Fleet
assumptions.value: 8 vehicles (base fleet from convex/seed.ts)
assumptions.why: vans, one bus, one ambulance; shift length 8 h

assumptions.name: Population
assumptions.value: 600 households sampled per seed from data/population.json when it exists (about 10% need a ride), otherwise 200 stand-in households from convex/seed.ts (about half need a ride)
assumptions.why: demo-scale zone: eight vehicles cannot serve the 11,855-household file in full, so each night uses a sampled zone

assumptions.name: Seeds
assumptions.value: each seed redraws the sampled population, vehicle start points, calls and cancellations
assumptions.why: ranges therefore reflect population and behavior variation

metricDefinitions.pickupsOnTime: Riders who needed a ride and finished boarding by their deadline (fire arrival minus 10 min). Primary metric. Higher is better.
metricDefinitions.pickupsLate: Boarded after the deadline but before the fire arrived. Higher is better.
metricDefinitions.ridersNeverPickedUp: Riders who needed a ride and were not aboard before the fire arrived, including ones no policy ever surfaced. Lower is better.
metricDefinitions.requests: Riders that reached the dispatcher before the fire arrived.
metricDefinitions.worstWaitMinutes: Longest time from a request surfacing to that rider finishing boarding, among riders picked up. Lower is better.
metricDefinitions.accessibleWaitMinutes: Mean wait for wheelchair and bedbound riders who were picked up (missing when none were). Lower is better.
metricDefinitions.vehicleMinutes: Total minutes vehicles spent on committed runs. Lower is better for the same pickups.
metricDefinitions.needers: Households in the night that truly needed a ride.

dispatchOnly.headline: Dispatch only, identical requests at identical times: change in on-time pickups, ortools minus heuristic, median -2.0 (5th to 95th percentile -6.0 to +0.0) across 100 paired seeds. On-time pickups, median: heuristic 63.5 (5th to 95th percentile 51.0 to 74.0), ortools 61.0 (5th to 95th percentile 49.0 to 69.0).

outreachOnly.headline: Outreach only, heuristic dispatcher on both sides: change in on-time pickups, ourOutreachRequests minus today911Requests, median +53.0 (5th to 95th percentile +44.0 to +64.0) across 100 paired seeds. On-time pickups, median: today911Requests 9.0 (5th to 95th percentile 6.0 to 14.0), ourOutreachRequests 63.5 (5th to 95th percentile 51.0 to 74.0).

combined.headline: Combined, today's process against outreach plus the optimizer: change in on-time pickups, ours minus today, median +56.0 (5th to 95th percentile +45.0 to +64.0) across 100 paired seeds. On-time pickups, median: today 5.0 (5th to 95th percentile 1.9 to 10.0), ours 61.0 (5th to 95th percentile 49.0 to 69.0).

todayProcess.headline: Today's process alone (911, first come first served, nearest unit) finished 5.0 (5th to 95th percentile 1.9 to 10.0) on-time pickups and left 54.0 (5th to 95th percentile 39.9 to 65.1) riders unpicked, out of 65 (5th to 95th percentile 52 to 75) riders who needed a ride, across 100 seeds.

whereWeDontHelp: With 4 vehicles our full process still leaves a median 9 of 64 riders unpicked (5th to 95th percentile 4 to 18); a dispatcher cannot send vans that do not exist. Dispatch only, the optimizer finished fewer on-time pickups than the heuristic at: fleetSize=4, hazardSpeed=0.5, hazardSpeed=0.7. It showed no clear difference at: fleetSize=6, fleetSize=8, fleetSize=12, answerRate=0.3, answerRate=0.6, answerRate=1.0, hazardSpeed=0.35, hazardSpeed=1.0, call911Lead=0.5, call911Lead=1.0, call911Lead=2.0, call911Lead=3.0.

exploration.label: Exploration, assumption-driven, not a finding
exploration.question: What happens if everyone leaves at once?

assumptions.name: Residents
assumptions.value: every household in data/population.json that has a car and no ride need drives one car (stand-in population: 20 cars per household)
assumptions.why: the whole area, not the sampled demo zone, because the question is about everyone

assumptions.name: Congestion cap
assumptions.value: volume over capacity is capped at 4.0
assumptions.why: stops the fourth-power BPR curve from producing absurd times when a single route is hugely overloaded

assumptions.name: Departure model
assumptions.value: dX = mu(t) dt + sigma dW, leave when X reaches 1
assumptions.why: drift-diffusion with two classes

assumptions.name: Evacuation-keen share
assumptions.why: stand-in; the plan cites Berkeley's survey of California evacuees for the two classes, shape not fitted here

assumptions.name: Keen drift and noise
assumptions.value: 0.1 per min, 0.1
assumptions.why: typical keen resident leaves in about 10 minutes

assumptions.name: Reluctant drift and noise
assumptions.value: 0.01 per min, 0.08
assumptions.why: typical reluctant resident would wait well over an hour on their own

assumptions.name: Fire pressure
assumptions.value: drift rises by up to 0.06 per min as the fire nears (scale 30 min)
assumptions.why: people leave faster as the fire gets close

assumptions.name: Forced departure
assumptions.value: everyone still home leaves at their deadline (fire arrival minus 10 min)
assumptions.why: keeps the model from stranding anyone

assumptions.name: Effect of a call
assumptions.value: a reached resident's drift rises by 0.05 per min from minute 5
assumptions.why: an assumption explored in simulation, not a finding

assumptions.name: Reached by a call
assumptions.value: probability equals the household's answer probability
assumptions.why: single attempt

assumptions.name: Destination
assumptions.value: every car drives the free-flow shortest path to the shelter
assumptions.why: a stand-in for real exit routes

assumptions.name: Edge capacity
assumptions.value: 600 vehicles per hour per lane
assumptions.why: residential street assumption

assumptions.name: Congestion
assumptions.value: BPR curve, 5 minute bins, 3 fixed-point iterations
assumptions.why: time on an edge depends on the volume entering in that bin

scenarioMeaning.withCalls: Same draws, but residents we reach get a drift boost (an assumption).
scenarioMeaning.everyoneAtOnce: Every resident leaves within 10 minutes of the warning.

exploration.headline: Exploration only: if every resident left within 10 minutes, the median trip to the shelter took 17 minutes against 6 with empty roads, and the busiest road segment ran at 33.2 times its capacity (drift-diffusion departures at their own pace: 12 minutes, 15.4 times). Median over 20 seeds; every input is an assumption.
